text.p: Following are the main stories in Wednesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- A 13-day blitz by police in areas surrounding the capital yielded half-a-tonne of drugs including 31 million ringgit worth of heroin and the arrest of 13 suspected traffickers, police said.
-- Petronas and Germany's BASF AG plan to jointly build and operate a $1 billion petrochemical complex in Pahang state.
-- Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said his 10-day visit to the U.S. and Japan has been successful in making known a high-technology area planned by Malaysia, the Multimedia Super Corridor.
-- Konsortium Perkapalan Bhd is looking to venture into the air cargo business, said its group executive chairman Mirzan Mahathir.
-- Malaysian Airlines plans to use the $120 million loan it acquired on Monday for working capital purposes and to repay some of the company's debts, said its treasury manager Low Chee Teng.
-- Sabah state is seeking the assistance of a neighbouring country to verify documents seized in a foiled bid to smuggle logs out of Malaysia using ships, said Sabah Chief Minister Yong Teck Lee.
